item.title: POLITICO Europe: Britain to keep tariffs on Chinese EVs ‘under review,’ UK business chief says
item.description: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the U.K.’s position on the issue was "finely balanced" as officials pursue talks with Brussels.

item.title: Euronews: Watch: mass Madrid protests over Maricarmen eviction and housing crisis
item.description: Protesters in Madrid have spent a second night camping in Puerta del Sol, turning the capital’s main square into a makeshift housing protest camp after the eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal, widely known as “Maricarmen”.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: UK business minister warns potential US diesel export ban ‘significant concern’
item.description: The U.K. receives around one-sixth of its diesel from the U.S. and would be one of the countries most exposed to an export ban.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: EU rejoin push risks causing uncertainty, warns business secretary
item.description: Jonathan Reynolds said the focus should be on improving Britain's trading relationship with Brussels.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Bill Gates says an AI ‘kill switch’ isn’t enough
item.description: The Microsoft co-founder called for mandatory monitoring of powerful artificial intelligence systems in an NBC interview that aired Sunday.

item.title: Euronews: Northern Ireland: 2,000 protesters block disputed Portadown march
item.description: Thousands of protesters blocked a road in Portadown, Northern Ireland, on 27 September, in an attempt to stop an Orange Order parade from entering the mainly Catholic and nationalist Garvaghy Road area.

item.title: Euronews: Sánchez vows to pass housing decree on Tuesday amid outrage over Maricarmen eviction
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has pledged to approve a housing decree on Tuesday following the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen from her home of 70 years, as protesters camp in Madrid's Puerta del Sol demanding stronger protections against evictions.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Burnham must be ‘selective’ in conference speech, says key ally
item.description: Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram, who has seen a draft of the PM's address, said there is "no way" he can cover all his arguments in one hour.

item.title: Euronews: How neutral should Switzerland be? Voters deliver decisive verdict
item.description: Supporters of the proposal, led by the right-wing Swiss People's Party (SVP), argued that Switzerland had moved too close to the European Union and NATO, particularly since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Euronews: Pope Leo XIV urges French Church to continue fight against sexual abuse
item.description: Speaking in Lourdes on Sunday morning, the Pope addressed the issue of sexual abuse within the Catholic Church, a closely watched aspect of his visit.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Euronews: Italy's fuel crisis: SOCAR announces price cap at IP stations
item.description: State-owned Azerbaijani group SOCAR is introducing a gradual price cap on the IP network after buying Italiana Petroli; from Monday a maximum price for petrol and diesel will also apply at ENI filling stations.

item.title: Euronews: Netanyahu battles October 7 warnings revelations with defiant UN speech
item.description: With Israel’s election approaching, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is battling new revelations of alleged warnings about Hamas’ 7 October attack and countered the political storm with a fiery UN speech directed at his voters and the world.

item.title: Euronews: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim seizure of second US underwater drone in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim that the vehicle is a REMUS 600 and has been handed over to Iranian military experts "to retrieve its data".

item.title: POLITICO Europe: EU Commission calls on countries to cut energy demands as costs surge
item.description: In a letter seen by POLITICO, Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen asked ministers to introduce new measures "in the context of constrained global supply."

item.title: Euronews: Serbia's politicians return to TV debates ahead of parliamentary election
item.description: A month before the early parliamentary elections, Serbia's high ranking politicians from the ruling and opposition parties engaged in a debate on the N1 channel after a prolonged boycott between the anti-government station and officials. The ownership change provided a new opportunity for dialogue.

item.title: Euronews: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market
item.description: Seven people were killed and 40 injured in a Saudi airstrike on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, as Houthi forces advance and Saudi-led air raids intensify.

item.title: Euronews: Collateral damage: How Cognac is paying the price for Europe’s trade wars
item.description: French Cognac producers are battling falling sales as trade disputes with China and the US squeeze the export-dependent industry and leave growers seeking EU support.

item.title: Euronews: Why Norwegians are buying more Chinese EVs despite growing scepticism
item.description: Electric cars account for more than 95% of new car registrations in Norway, the highest share in the world. About one in four new EVs registered there are from fully or partly Chinese-owned brands.

item.title: Euronews: Are you in pain? In some cases, exercising may be as good as painkillers
item.description: From pilates to tai chi, even modest amounts of exercise can relieve pain as effectively as common pain medicines, opening the door to holistic therapeutic approaches, according to a new study.

item.title: Euronews: Ireland team to wear black armbands as players vote to go ahead with Israel game
item.description: The Israeli FA issued a statement commending the FAI and the Irish squad for deciding to go ahead with the match, saying: "Football has won."

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Swiss say no to hardening neutrality principle, safeguarding sanctions on Russia
item.description: The Kremlin backed the referendum proposal, which was opposed by the Swiss government.

item.title: Euronews: Etna erupts again: chaos at Catania airport, risk of higher air fares
item.description: Mount Etna has resumed volcanic activity. Flights to and from Catania are suspended until Sunday because of ash. Unions protest over disruption caused by diverted services to other Sicilian airports.

item.title: Euronews: At least two people were killed and 19 are in hospital after a bus crashed near Munich
item.description: The bus, which was on its way to Munich's beer festival and was carrying approximately 35 Filipino tourists, crashed at 05:41 a.m., according to local authorities.

item.title: Euronews: How Russia recruits Belarusians for war in Ukraine: Methods and consequences
item.description: Russia's recruitment drive targeting Belarusians has become a key tool to boost manpower on the battlefield and exploits economic hardship and isolation.

item.title: Euronews: EU tells countries to curb energy demand as gas prices face winter squeeze
item.description: Energy Commissioner Jørgensen warned capitals that the EU is not facing an immediate gas-security crisis, but it is facing a price-and-supply squeeze that could become more difficult as winter approaches, according to a letter seen by Euronews.

item.title: Euronews: Ethiopia’s army chief accuses Egypt and Sudan of backing armed alliance seeking to oust Abiy Ahmed
item.description: Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia is drawing in the country’s disputes with Egypt, Sudan and Eritrea, raising fears that its internal conflict could spread across the region.

item.title: Euronews: Protesters camp in Madrid in demonstration against Spain' housing crisis
item.description: Around 150 tents now occupy Madrid's Puerta del Sol after Saturday's protest over 87-year-old Maricarmen's eviction. Protesters, mobilised by the Tenants' Union, demand a housing decree on Tuesday: "Either rentierism falls or the government".

item.title: Euronews: Poland and Lithuania preparing cross-border evacuation plan for Baltic states
item.description: The Suwałki gap, a strip of territory linking Poland and Lithuania - and therefore connecting the Baltic states with other NATO allies and the rest of the European Union - is of particular importance to the plan.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Northern Ireland standoff puts peace and power-sharing at risk
item.description: A sudden revival of the 1990s confrontations between Orange Order marchers and Catholic demonstrators puts the police back in the middle — and leaders of Northern Ireland’s supposed unity government on opposite sides.

item.title: Euronews: 'A theft from citizens': Spain hits 1,000 days without a new budget
item.description: The Spanish Ministry of Finance insists that a budget will soon be put forward for 2027. "We are confident it will be approved and we are not contemplating any other scenario," sources told Euronews.

item.title: Euronews: Discount store sparks revolution on Sylt, reshaping the island of the rich
item.description: The German island Sylt has long battled acute housing shortages and locals being pushed out. Now, of all things, a discount chain offers a remedy: Lidl is building a completely new housing complex in Tinnum.

item.title: Euronews: Watch live: Pope Leo XIV in Lourdes as visit to France continues
item.description: The pontiff is due to meet with victims of clerical sex abuse in Lourdes before travelling on to Metz in northeastern France on Monday.
